references.text: Mica had established a sanctuary and made an ephod and household gods, and appointed one of his sons as priest—this forms the background for the unlawful idolatry that the tribe of Dan continued.
Jonathan and the carved image were taken by the Danites from Mica's house, and Jonathan was persuaded to become priest for the tribe of Dan.
Gershom was a son of Moses, and Jonathan descended from him—this confirms the lineage mentioned in the verse.
Gershom is mentioned as Moses' son, and his descendants served at the tabernacle—in contrast to Jonathan's idolatrous priesthood.
Jeroboam set up golden calves in Dan and Bethel and appointed priests who were not from the tribe of Levi—Dan remained a center for idol worship.
Assyria carried Israel away into exile—this may be the 'captivity of the land' to which the verse refers.
The Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser took Dan and other cities and led the people to Assyria—a possible reference to the captivity of the land.
The ark of the covenant was taken by the Philistines—another event in which holy objects were carried away, which may relate to the 'captivity of the land'.
